discovery: Development of next-generation DNA sequencing (sequencing by synthesis with reversible-terminator chemistry), which enabled massively parallel, low-cost genome sequencing
rationale: After biology-adjacent awards in 2024 (protein design and structure prediction) and a materials award in 2025 (MOFs), the committee is likely to return to chemistry that changed the life sciences. Solexa/Illumina sequencing by synthesis is a chemical invention built on fluorescent reversible terminators and surface cluster amplification. It has made genomics routine across medicine and biology. Its inventors have already won the Breakthrough Prize, the Millennium Technology Prize and other major awards that often come before a Nobel.
